name: 24-pounder service charge
notes: A separate assembly SO THE GUN CAN BE RELOADED (Robin): the charge is consumed and ceases to exist, the shot is transferred out, the gun persists. A service charge for a 24-pounder was about a third of the shot's weight — 8 lb of powder to 24 lb of ball — here 3.629 kg. ★ The powder is THREE PARTS, not one material: black powder is a mechanical mixture of potassium nitrate, charcoal and sulfur at 75/15/10, and its bulk properties DERIVE from them (see `materials::mixture_tests`). Modelling it as one substance would have meant inventing a specific heat, which is exactly what was backed out on 2026-08-02. The wad is what holds the ball against the charge and is the reason a gun could be fired downhill. ★★ The powder parts carry a PACKING FRACTION, which is the honest form of a thing the catalogue already half-said. Their SHAPES are the envelope — the space the charge fills in the chamber, 3629 cm3 — and `packing` 0.511 says how much of that envelope is substance. Mass is envelope x packing x density, so it comes out right while the chamber volume ALSO comes out right, and the gap between the two is the ~49% void of corned powder. That matters rather than being cosmetic: chamber volume sets the pressure the burn reaches. ★ The packing is DERIVED, not typed: it is the poured bulk density of corned powder (1000 kg/m3) over the mixture's own true density (1957 kg/m3, volume-weighted from the three constituents exactly as `materials::mixture_tests` computes it). A first version of this file sized the parts to their SOLID volume and under-stated the chamber by half.
